title: Kevon Looney agrees to sign 1-year, $3.9 million deal with Lakers
content:
Veteran center Kevon Looney has agreed to sign a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Los Angeles Lakers, Looney’s agent, Todd Ramasar, confirmed to The Athletic on Tuesday.

Looney, 30, was an unrestricted free agent who last played for the New Orleans Pelicans. He is a three-time NBA champion with the Golden State Warriors (in 2017, 2018, 2022) who served as a key role player known for his rebounding. ESPN was first to report the news of his deal with the Lakers.

In the wake of the Lakers’ stunning decision to land 24-year-old big man Walker Kessler via a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz last week, Looney gives the Lakers more frontcourt depth at a time when size is sorely needed to contend in the West. Whether it’s the San Antonio Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama, the Oklahoma City Thunder’s Chet Holmgren, the Denver Nuggets’ Nikola Jokić, the Minnesota Timberwolves’ Rudy Gobert or the Houston Rockets’ Alperen Şengün, there is no shortage of excellent big men in the conference.

The Lakers made it their top priority to add an elite rim protector this offseason — one who complements franchise centerpiece Luka Dončić and whose career timeline sets them up for a long-term partnership. They believe they did just that when they paid a steep price for Kessler (a four-year, $130 million deal, in addition to sending two first-round draft picks and two first-round pick swaps to the Jazz).

Two days after doing that deal, they sent center Deandre Ayton to the Washington Wizards for guard Jaden Hardy and the Wizards’ second-round picks in 2031 and 2032. The 27-year-old Ayton started 72 games for the Lakers last season, averaging 12.5 points and eight rebounds before his production dipped in the playoffs (he averaged just 7.3 points and 7.8 rebounds in a second-round loss to Oklahoma City).

While Kessler is a clear upgrade over Ayton as the starting center, the fact remains that he played just five games last season (because of a torn labrum in his left shoulder) and just 58 games the season before that. Adding Looney gives the Lakers depth on that front, although he is also coming off an injury-riddled 2025-26 (he played just 21 games because of a left knee injury). Looney has been one of the league’s most durable performers for the majority of his career, playing at least 74 games in each of the four previous seasons (including all 82 games twice). He has more championship experience than anyone on the Lakers’ roster now, as well.

The Lakers weighed other options before signing Looney. League sources, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, indicated that veteran big man Andre Drummond was among the players they considered (he signed with the New York Knicks). The Lakers are also known to be in pursuit of 23-year-old swingman Jonathan Kuminga, who had his team option ($24.3 million) declined by the Atlanta Hawks and is among the top unrestricted free agents left on the market.

— Dan Woike contributed to this report
